case_prompt:
A 37-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus presented with a 4-month history of daily, persistent, and progressively worsening pulsulsatile bitemporal headaches accompanied by photophobia, without nausea, vomiting, or phonophobia. One week prior to evaluation, she noticed new weakness in her right arm. Her home medications included prednisone 40 mg daily, azathioprine 50 mg twice daily, and hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily. Family history was unremarkable.

On physical examination, blood pressure was 115/77 mmHg, heart rate 80 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, and axillary temperature 36.2 C. An erythematous rash was present over the bilateral malar areas of the face. Neurological examination revealed that she was alert and oriented to person, place, and time, with fluent speech. Pupils were equal, round, and reactive to light and accommodation bilaterally. Fundoscopic examination showed sharp optic discs without papilledema. Other cranial nerves were intact. Motor examination showed 5/5 strength throughout all four extremities with symmetric, normal reflexes. Sensation was intact, gait was normal, and there was no nuchal rigidity.

Laboratory evaluation demonstrated a hemoglobin of 13.3 g/dL, hematocrit 40%, leukocyte count 7,143/mm^3, platelet count 223,300/mm^3, serum creatinine 0.78 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen 10 mg/dL, sodium 141 mEq/L, potassium 3.7 mEq/L, magnesium 2.09 mg/dL, ionized calcium 1.26 mmol/L, and C-reactive protein 2.4 mg/dL.

Non-contrast computed tomography of the head demonstrated a left extra-axial parietooccipital focal hypoattenuation associated with adjacent calvarial bone erosion. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging of the brain revealed a left parietooccipital subdural collection associated with focal leptomeningeal thickening.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Bacterial Subdural Empyema with Calvarial Osteomyelitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in an immunosuppressed lupus patient presenting with an extra-axial fluid collection and adjacent skull erosion, but ruled out intraoperatively by the absence of frank purulence and sterile bacterial cultures.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Neurosurgery was consulted and recommended craniotomy for evacuation of the subdural collection. During the procedure, the collection was not purulent, which raised no concerns for subdural empyema.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given active SLE with malar rash presenting with chronic headache, focal motor deficit, and leptomeningeal enhancement, but excluded by surgical biopsy demonstrating granulomatous fungal infection rather than immune complex pachymeningitis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The adjacent dura mater was resected showing noncaseous granuloma with multinucleated giant cells and asteroids bodies on histopathology [Figure 3]. In addition rounded birefringent structures with positive silver stain consistent with PCM were noticed.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Confirmed during craniotomy and dural resection by histopathological demonstration of noncaseating granulomas containing multinucleated giant cells, asteroid bodies, and silver-stain-positive rounded birefringent yeast forms characteristic of Paracoccidioides, leading to complete clinical and radiological recovery on 12 months of oral itraconazole.

In addition rounded birefringent structures with positive silver stain consistent with PCM were noticed. Infectious disease was consulted and itraconazole was started 200 mg daily for 12 months. After procedure, the patient showed improvement of headache and of the weakness.
